    <p><strong>This is an active draft.</strong></p>
    <p>Agentic machine learning systems are systems in which a foundation model works toward a goal over many steps, using memory to carry state and tools to act on software, data, and services outside itself. Engineering them means managing the whole trajectory of observations, decisions, and actions rather than a single request, because each trajectory must stay within bounds while it runs, survive the failure of any step, and end in work that someone can check.</p>
    <p>This book develops the principles for building such systems in the order their dependencies impose. It begins with the model call and the cost of reasoning at inference time, then builds memory from the context window and KV cache to persistent stores. It adds tools through typed interfaces, sandboxed execution, and security controls, and places the agent inside a runtime that supervises long-running work, recovers from failure, and evaluates results. It then shows how verified trajectories become training data for fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, and how agents that work together are coordinated and costed per accepted task.</p>

## What You Will Learn {.unnumbered}

The book opens with an introduction that defines the agentic system and its unit of work, the trajectory, and the three exposures an agent adds beyond a single model call: horizon, state, and authority. Seven parts then build the system in order:

- **Part I: The Model** studies the foundation model through a single call, what it reads, returns, and costs, and when spending more inference on one decision raises the evidence behind it.
- **Part II: Agent Memory** closes the state exposure through context engineering, KV cache management, and long-term memory with retrieval.
- **Part III: Tool Use** closes the authority exposure through tool calling that settles an uncertain effect before any retry, sandboxes that contain the code behind it, and security controls against untrusted input that steers legitimate access.
- **Part IV: The Agent Runtime** closes the horizon exposure through the agent harness, durable execution, and failure recovery, and ends with agent evaluation and operation, because nothing should be trained before it can be measured.
- **Part V: Learning from Trajectories** changes the model, when evaluation shows that cheaper fixes do not remove a failure, through trajectory curation, trajectory fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards.
- **Part VI: Agents at Scale** multiplies all three exposures through multi-agent coordination and prices the system per accepted task in agent economics.
- **Part VII: Synthesis** runs one trajectory through every part and ends at the specification boundary, the work that stays with the engineer.

:::
